Question: Let \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) be digits with \(a\ne0.\) The three-digit integer \(\overline{abc}\) lies one third of the way from the square of a positive integer to the square of the next larger integer. The integer \(\overline{acb}\) lies two thirds of the way between the same two squares. What is \(a+b+c?\)
Solution:
The two integers are separated by one third of the gap between the squares. Interchanging their last two digits also gives a useful expression for that separation.

Let the lower square be \(n^2\), where \(n\) is a positive integer. The gap to the next square is \((n+1)^2-n^2=2n+1\), so
\[
\overline{abc}=n^2+\frac{2n+1}{3},\qquad
\overline{acb}=n^2+\frac{2(2n+1)}{3}.
\]
On the other hand, decimal place value gives
\[
\overline{acb}-\overline{abc}
=(100a+10c+b)-(100a+10b+c)=9(c-b).
\]
Equating the two expressions for the difference yields
\[
2n+1=27(c-b).
\]
Thus the square gap is an odd multiple of \(27\).

Because \(100\leq\overline{abc}\leq999\) and it lies strictly between \(n^2\) and \((n+1)^2\), we have \(10\leq n\leq31\). Consequently,
\[
21\leq2n+1\leq63.
\]
The only odd multiple of \(27\) in this interval is \(27\). Therefore \(n=13\), and
\[
\overline{abc}=169+9=178.
\]
Its digit interchange is \(187=169+18\), which verifies the second condition between \(169\) and \(196\). Hence \(a+b+c=1+7+8=16\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
